questions.question: Approximately how old is Earth?
choices: 4.6 million years
460 thousand years
46 billion years
4.6 billion years

questions.question: What process built the early Earth from smaller solid bodies?
choices: Accretion
Photosynthesis
Evapotranspiration
Chemical digestion

questions.question: What is planetary differentiation?
choices: Mixing all planetary materials into one uniform layer
Separation of planetary material into layers according to properties such as density
Cooling only the surface without any internal redistribution
Breaking a planet into separate orbiting pieces

questions.question: Which early organisms contributed greatly to rising atmospheric oxygen through photosynthesis?
choices: Flowering plants
Dinosaurs
Cyanobacteria
Early mammals

questions.question: Which era follows the Mesozoic and includes the present?
choices: Paleozoic Era
Archean Eon
Hadean Eon
Cenozoic Era

questions.question: Which major interval is especially associated with the dominance of non-avian dinosaurs?
choices: Mesozoic Era
Cenozoic Era
Hadean Eon
Archean Eon

questions.question: What is a mass extinction?
choices: The death of one individual organism
A geologically rapid loss of many species across the world
A seasonal decrease in one local population
The movement of all species into one habitat

questions.question: Why did dense iron-rich material move toward Earth's center during early differentiation?
choices: It rose because greater density always produces buoyancy
It remained entirely at the surface because of its mass
It sank relative to less dense material when conditions allowed flow
It mixed uniformly because gravity cannot separate materials

questions.question: Why was rising oxygen a major change for early life?
choices: It immediately created all modern animal groups
It prevented organisms from using energy in cells
It affected only rocks, with no consequences for life
It enabled new metabolic possibilities while harming some oxygen-intolerant organisms

questions.question: How did an ozone layer affect opportunities for life on land?
choices: It reduced exposure to harmful ultraviolet radiation
It supplied all the nutrients needed in soil
It caused land to form for the first time
It eliminated the need for water in living cells

questions.question: Why do matching ancient rocks across separated continents support past continental connection?
choices: Every rock everywhere has the same age
Their ages and structures can record a shared geological history
Oceans cannot form between continents
Rock color alone identifies an identical history

questions.question: What evidence strongly supports a major asteroid impact at the end of the Cretaceous?
choices: The regular occurrence of ocean tides
The presence of modern mountain glaciers alone
A large dated impact crater and a widespread iridium-rich boundary layer
The shape of modern rivers unrelated to that boundary

questions.question: How can a mass extinction affect later evolution?
choices: All survivors must retain the same ecological roles forever
It makes surviving populations lose all inherited variation
It guarantees immediate return of the extinct species
Surviving groups may diversify into newly available ecological roles

questions.question: Why are the earliest parts of Earth's history harder to reconstruct from surface rocks?
choices: Many early rocks were altered, destroyed, or recycled
Early Earth rocks formed without minerals
Every early surface remained undisturbed
All surface rocks record the same interval equally well

questions.question: How have ice ages affected landscapes?
choices: Ice ages prevented all erosion
Glaciers eroded and deposited material as ice advanced and retreated
Glaciers made every continent flat
Ice ages changed rock atoms into air

questions.question: Which sequence places these events from earliest to latest?
choices: Dinosaurs appear, Earth forms, humans appear, oxygen rises
Humans appear, oxygen rises, Earth forms, dinosaurs appear
Earth forms, atmospheric oxygen rises, dinosaurs appear, humans appear
Oxygen rises, humans appear, dinosaurs appear, Earth forms

questions.question: An ancient marine fossil is found in rock now high in a mountain range. What history is supported?
choices: The ocean must have covered the mountain at its present height
The fossil was made by modern snowfall
The mountain has remained unchanged since Earth's formation
The material formed in a marine setting and was later uplifted

questions.question: Earth existed for billions of years before abundant animal fossils appeared. What does this imply?
choices: Much of Earth's history predates familiar animal life
Earth and animals formed at exactly the same time
All early life was a modern mammal
Rocks can form only after animals appear

questions.question: Two regions now far apart share matching rocks from when Pangaea existed. Which explanation fits plate tectonics?
choices: Both regions remained fixed while only seawater moved
The regions were once closer and later moved apart
Identical ages alone prove every rock formed in one place
The rocks formed only after the continents reached their current positions

questions.question: A boundary layer records abrupt species losses, followed by new groups in younger layers. What pattern does this support?
choices: No biological change through time
Simultaneous origin of every fossil species
An extinction event followed by diversification
A complete absence of environmental change
